text_fidelity_a:
Michelin A1 Aircomp Ultralight Fahrrad Schlauch 28´´ I bought two of these at Performance bike shop because they were on sale. Smooth stems looked nice.
Both of them came apart at the seam. One lasted a few miles from home, another lasted little longer but otherwise more walking distance to home. I had a patch kit and a pump but no use. At least I got refund when took them back to the store. I explained the store clerk what had happened and he wasn't even surprised.
I had different brands of tubes mostly cheap store brand in the past but nothing compare to this. I was very surprised because this happened to well-known name.
What I learned from this. 1) Don't buy anything says ultra light. 2) Don't buy anything only because it's a well-known brand name, it was probably made by another company.
I weigh 140lbs, so the weight wasn't an issue, just in case you are wondering. I inflated it 120psi. Size of the tire was 700x20c.
You can avoid pinch flat snake bites by inflating the tire to certain pressure. If the tire picks up a broken staple, it gets flat but you can patch it. When the tube comes apart, you can't do anything specially if the spare you happen to have has the same defect.

I'll never buy it and I don't recommend this to anybody.
text_fidelity_b: Michelin A1 Aircomp Ultralight Fahrrad Schlauch 28´´

Coleman ComfortSmart Suspension Camping Chair After a month-long search for a balcony chair while visiting too many different stores, I finally found this one at BJ's for $39.99. It is a dream to sit in because the material has a lot of give which makes it very comfortable. What I also like is:

- it has a high back and a slight recline to it
- there's a small cup holder (more for a soda can than anything else) that easily folds out from under the right side of the seat
- it appears to be built very sturdy
- it opens with ease
- the arm rests are comfortable and covered in foam
- the chair comes in a nice carrying bag
- the back (which looks white in the picture on Amazon) is actually clear mesh; like a pair of black pantyhose but very strong.

The only negatives are that the chair is heavy, very tall and has a large footprint. Originally, I purchased two of these but because of the large footprint was only able to fit one comfortably on the available space on my balcony. The fact that I kept only one of these chairs when I wanted to keep two speaks volumes since I only buy chairs in pairs. However, this is the most comfortable lawn/balcony/beach chair I ever sat in in my life so forget about any potential visitor he or she can stand on the balcony during a visit instead.

By the way, I must have tried over 30 beach and other folding chairs before I found this one. In fact, I purchased a total of 3 different chairs (in sets of 2) in a state of desperation and took all of them back except for this one. The two Lifetime Comfort folding chairs I purchased at BJs for $19.99 were exceptionally sturdy but too clinical looking even though they were relatively comfortable for a straight-backed chair. After returning those, I purchased 2 Picnic Time Portable Folding Sports Chairs in Hunter Green for $39.99 each at TJ Maxx. I almost kept those but when I saw these I bought 2 at BJs for $39.99 each and compared them to the comfort of the Picnic Time chairs. The Coleman won by a long shot. If I had the room, I would have kept the second suspension chair as a backup. I hope this chair lasts a long, long time and is actually as sturdy as it feels.

This was a great buy!
text_fidelity_b: Coleman ComfortSmart Suspension Camping Chair

text_fidelity_a:
ENO - Eagles Nest Outfitters HouseFly Rain Tarp, Ultralight Camping Tarp I liked this fly after watching a few videos online. I decided to purchase the HouseFly vs. others. I loved that it has ends that can be closed off or rolled back, and the larger size of the HouseFly was my main reason for purchasing it.

I received mine yesterday and promptly went about setting it up outside. I wanted a fair test before heading out on the trail. Last night was a superb choice as it was to rain, and it did. I remained totally dry. I needed the unpack and set up once before heading out, and I recommend that to anyone. It helped wipe out some rough edges on my setup technique.

Setup was easy for my first time. We worked at a rather moderate pace, especially when my 8-year old wanted to help put in the stakes for the tie-down ropes. The stakes are not included in the fly and must be purchased separately. I chose the orange-colored fly over the green as it makes the fly easier seen. After setting up my fly, I promptly forgot the first rule, walk further away from the tie-down cordage and stakes. Where I immediately tripped myself up.

I was not rather impressed with the included tie-down cordage. It is rather stiff, and I prefer ropes which are easily bendable and packable. Not to mention easier to stake out. So, I will be replacing the cordage with some paracord with a softer, more pliable body. This is the first real con I have had with ENO products. But to be totally fair to them, I almost always find that cordage included with a product doesn't live up to my personal desires/expectations. You may find the cordage fine and have no issue with it. I also wanted a slightly longer length on the ridge ties. The cordage may be fine after some initial usage, but in my usage, the cordage was just as stiff upon taking down the fly as it was putting it up.

I would still repurchase the HouseFly in a moment, with or without the cordage. I will indeed be buying it again for the wife and her hammock, though I think I'll choose a green or blue version for her. Doing so will allow me to switch out my color as my mood fits. I'll likely buy something smaller for the kids.

Oh, It's rather large, I think we could safely hang side by side under the fly.

edit 12/28/2017

Yes, two people can hang under the fly though I set it up slightly wider than usual. I ended up not being able to close the doors. I didn't want to adjust my setup. It rained the evening, and the fly kept up perfectly dry all night.
text_fidelity_b: ENO - Eagles Nest Outfitters HouseFly Rain Tarp, Ultralight Camping Tarp

text_fidelity_a: Franklin Sports Full Size Hard Court Portable Basketball System My teenagers have been wanting a basketball hoop for a while. This one seems to be a nice quality one. It came with a couple of little wrenches to put it together, but my husband used his own socket set which made it a little easier. He put it together by himself, but he said it would definitely be easier with a second person. You can adjust the height, but it's not something you would do frequently. Some others have a lever that you can use to change the height. This one requires you to unscrew the screw and then adjust the tube (within a tube - telescoping). It's kind of like the pop up tents, except instead of the button you have to press, you have to unscrew the screw. It would be much easier to have a second person to help you if you are changing heights.  My husband found it easier to put the whole thing on the side to adjust the height. There are wheels on the bottom of the base so you can move it if needed. We have a two door garage and have it placed against the brick between the doors. It fits well and doesn't interfere with our cars.

I really love the lid they designed for this, it is super easy to drink from any angle unlike yeti tumblers where it can leak if the opening isn't aligned with your mouth perfectly, and it is also capable of higher flow than most other stainless cup lids which is great if you are really thirsty after working out. I also like that the cup is dishwasher safe, unlike most stainless cups which recommend hand washing.. and the lid is very easy to clean also and doesn't seem prone to collecting mold even when used with sugary drinks. Some other reviewers have complained about the lid leaking but in my experience it is really easy to prevent as long as you make sure to close it all the way, which isn't difficult.

The only thing I really don't care for about this bottle is the loud branding, even though Gatorade is a brand which I like, I don't enjoy feeling like a walking advertisement and it also makes the bottle seem a little out of place when used in a non-sports setting. That said, I like the lid design on this bottle so much that my other stainless cups have been collecting dust since I got this one.

text_fidelity_a:
Franklin Sports Portable Backyard Croquet Sets - Complete 4 + 6 Player Croquet Sets with Mallets, Croquet Balls + Wickets Included - Outdoor Family Lawn Game Sets with Carry Bag This set includes:
- Six (6) all weather colored balls of one color of each (red, yellow, orange, blue, green, and black).
- Nine (9) all weather plastic coated metal wickets.
- Six (6) solid wood mallets with wooden handles (30.75 inches assembled) --one for each color. They have double metal locking joints and assembly is required each time.
- Two (2) 24" wooden stakes with colored lines that match the colors of the balls and mallet handles. NOTE that I received four (4) wooden stakes in my package (see picture).
- One carry case.
- One paltry instruction sheet.

I had always wanted to play croquet and this is my first set. When I first opened the package, I was really impressed and considered this five stars for the price since it contains everything needed to play. In order to store all the items in the carry case, the set must be disassembled each time after play. What I mean by this is that the wooden handles have to be screwed and unscrewed from the mallet head. Since I live in a condo, I cannot leave this set assembled after playing as I have no garage to store this in and I have to remove the wickets from the complex's lawn when done with the game.

After watching some how-to videos, my boyfriend and I played this. We had a lot of fun as it is a cross between golf and bocce ball to me.

It was during play that we noticed a problem with this set. The biggest issue is that each wood mallet with its associated handle kept loosening up no matter how hard we tightened it. Several times we had to re-tighten the mallets. Also, after our game was over, we noticed that the plastic coating on the wickets was chipping off on the bottom and exposing the metal and this was the first time we used the set. I suppose this is to be expected, however..

Overall, we enjoyed this game and the set seems to be good quality with the exception of the mallet head and its associated handle loosening up. It is for this reason only I rate this 3.4 stars. A really professional set would be more than double the price of this one. If I were in the market for a higher end set, I would look into this [[ASIN:B073YFZY9M Amish-made croquet set]].
text_fidelity_b: Franklin Sports Portable Backyard Croquet Sets - Complete 4 + 6 Player Croquet Sets with Mallets, Croquet Balls + Wickets Included - Outdoor Family Lawn Game Sets with Carry Bag

text_fidelity_a: WILSON Pro Staff Team Tennis Racket, 4 3/8", Black/White I play a LOT of tennis and am trying to improve my game through personal, regular lessons, and a lot of team practice and matches.  I play doubles and singles and am very serious about the game.  That said, I'm giving this racquet 5 stars for now.  I've only played with it a couple of times but each time was fairly long.  I played with it today in a friendly singles tennis match against a woman whom I practice with, and is at least a 4.0 player.  So far I like it.  The strings are factory strings and are very tight - very little if any give even when hitting hard.  I will probably get a good set of Prince strings put on it later on.  It's a little heavier than my Head Ti.s6 (very light) and the weight seems to be mainly in the top part of the racquet head.  That's good because  I can get some extra down motion going in my serve thus more power.  It has more power than my Head and I am still learning to keep it under control.  I find my serves are going a little faster and deeper with this racquet than with my Head racquet.  I also use to play with a Prince O3 racquet but found it to be on the heavy side - the Wilson Pro Staff is much lighter.  My singles practice partner wanted to play with it today and she really loved it.  It took her a while to get her serves where she usually places them but after about an hour of playing she was into this racquet.  My coach took a look at this racquet and seemed to like it pretty good but didn't try it out.  This review is from a female perspective and we don't usually hit as hard as men, so the review might not be as useful to you if you're male with a powerful stroke.  The racquet I received for review has a grip size of 4 3/8" and I normally use a  4 1/4, but the 4 3/8 felt fine and I made good, well placed  solid strokes with it. I might even move up to the a 4 3/8" later on.  In conclusion, I think this would be a very good racquet for a man or woman and the price is reasonable (as of this review it costs $139.00).  It's seems to be solid, well-constructed and well balanced (except for maybe the extra weight in the head but that really didn't seem to bother me in the least and it helped my serves.)

19Pcs Resistance Bands Set Workout Bands - 4 Pull Up Bands, 3 Exercise Resistance Loop Bands, 2 Core Sliders, Jump Rope, Handles, Door Anchor, Wrist Wraps for Body Stretching/Power Training I am a senior, and was exercising religiously at a fitness center, prior to the virus. I won't be going back.
We live in a senior condo, and I have no space for fitness hardware.

After almost three months of not exercising, I was getting depressed, and purchased an inexpensive set of bands from Amazon. My only prior expensive with bands was a short rehab stint for a frozen shoulder and stiff neck.

Being new to bands, I didn't know what to get,.
The inexpensive bands I bought, didn't do much for me.

I found there are three primary types of resistance bands.
The open ended rubber hose style, that can have handles attached,
The closed loop design. This product being reviewed is closed loop.
The very wide open ended bands I used in rehab. Those are very flexible and can be used open, or knotted. They don't seem to be widely available.

After buying the open ended rubber hose style, I started exercising in front of You Tube Fitness videos. In my case, senior fitness videos. Although I'm a male, I use the Senior Fitness with Meredith, exercise. No products are advertised for sale on the site. I quickly saw the advantage in having different sets of bands. There is also an advantage in having different lengths. Different exercises utilize the open ended rubber hose style, while others lend themselves to the closed loop. The thicker closed loop bands seem safer for lower body exercises. I first used the thinner rubber type bands for lower body exercises. One slipped off my foot, and boomeranged back into my throat. Ouch.

Having different sets keeps you from wasting time by having to stop and change your bands, such as removing handles and tying loops during exercises, and then untying them. Just switch to the right band.

This product being reviewed has closed loops, of varied resistance. Depending on your level of fitness, they can wear you out as you change to thicker bands. A few items in this set were an overkill for me. I won't use the jump rope or the sliders. The sliders are useful though for moving furniture. They are the same size as the large sliders I keep under my sofa, for ease of moving. The quality of the bands that come with this product seem excellent.

The items in this product can easily be returned to the original bag, taking up almost no space. Don't rip the box as it also comes in handy for storage.

Finally, if you are new to bands, I suggest watching some videos utilizing different bands, and starting with the type that appeals to you.
text_fidelity_b: 19Pcs Resistance Bands Set Workout Bands - 4 Pull Up Bands, 3 Exercise Resistance Loop Bands, 2 Core Sliders, Jump Rope, Handles, Door Anchor, Wrist Wraps for Body Stretching/Power Training

text_fidelity_a:
GLIDING DISCS ULTIMATE BUNS AND LEGS WORKOUT AS SEEN ON TV I have done gliding-type moves in other workouts and enjoyed them, so I was eager to try this set. The term Gliding is trademarked by fitness instructor Mindy Mylrea, and this is the original set of 3 workouts on one disk sold via infomercial. The workouts including Ultimate Buns and Legs, Fat Burning Cardio, and Total Body Workout. This set also includes two gliding discs designed for use on carpet (discs for use on smooth flooring are sold elsewhere).

The Ultimate Buns & Legs workout is an approximately 35-minute workout focused on the lower body. It begins with a 6-minute warm-up which includes shoulder rolls, squats (moving side-to-side with discs under the feet), and stretches. About 10 minutes of standing leg work follows: you will do single leg squats, first to either side, then to the rear, and then move into double leg squats. This segment includes a 2-minute stretch before moving to the floor. The floor work includes bridge moves (with the discs under your heels), side and plank work, and finally, some brief back extensions for a total of about 15 minutes. The workout ends with a 4-minute seated stretch which includes twists. Overall, I liked this workout; I felt that it gave me a bit of a cardio effect, and I felt a slight soreness in the backs of my legs the next day.

Fat Burning Cardio is a 37-minute aerobic interval workout which alternates 4-6 minute cardio intervals with 3-minute toning segments using the discs. The workout begins with a 6.5 minute warm-up which includes side steps, hamstring curls, and knee lifts; the warm-up ends with squats and lunges using the discs. The first cardio interval is about 4 minutes and includes marches with a V-step, eventually adding on mambos and small hops (I recognized music from Firm videos here). The first toning segment consists of squats and single leg lunges; the lunges are performed both to the side and to the back, moving from a slow to fast tempo. The next cardio segment is a little longer at about 6 minutes, and it includes side steps with a direction change, adding jumping jacks, lunges with a hop, and heel digs with a hop; my calves were really burning during this segment! In the toning segment which follows, you will do circle lunges (using the disc around one foot and making a circle around the other disk), and slow side squats remaining in a crouched position. The final cardio interval is 5 minutes long and starts with a chasse/lunge combo, adding scoops and jogs. The last gliding segment has more side squats as well as a back-side-back lunge combination. This workout finishes with a 5-minute stretch which targets the hamstrings, thighs, and hip flexors. Again, I felt some soreness from this workout the next day (mainly in my calves), but I was a bit disappointed that my heart rate was only in my target zone for less than 20 minutes.

The final workout in this set is the Total Body Workout, a 54-minute workout targeting the entire body. The 6.5-minute warm-up is similar to the ones above, featuring side steps with shoulder rolls and squats using the disks. The next part of the workout is 29.5 minutes of standing leg work. Again, the moves are similar to those done in the above two workouts--eg, squats, single leg lunges, circle lunges, etc.--but for some reason, I enjoyed them more here. A brief standing stretch follows before moving on to the floor work, which begins with an additional 2-minute stretch in a seated position. Next comes 5 minutes of abs work on your back, using the discs both under the heels and under the hands. Following this comes 5 minutes of side-lying work, about 7 minutes of bride and very tough plank work (again using the disks both under the hands and under the feet), and finally, a 4-minute floor stretch. I particularly enjoyed the standing portion of this workout (which actually put me in my target HR zone for over 20 minutes), and I felt more soreness in my legs the next day than I did with the Ultimate Buns & Legs workout.

Overall, I liked these workouts a lot, and I think getting them together on one DVD is a great deal. I find gliding to be a lot of fun, and use of the discs definitely seems to work my muscles in unique ways (for example, I felt my inner thighs working much more than usual). I would definitely recommend this set, and I give it a rating of 4 1/2 stars.
text_fidelity_b: GLIDING DISCS ULTIMATE BUNS AND LEGS WORKOUT AS SEEN ON TV

Britax Child Bike Seat (Prior Model) Britax has been making things for children for a very long time and it enjoys a strong reputation as a company that produces quality products. The high regard myself and others have for Britax was enough to convince me to obtain this bicycle seat and I have not regretted my decision.

I have two small girls, one of whom is still small enough to use a seat such as this. The weight limit is 40 pounds, so it is only going to work for children roughly four years of age or younger. My little one is still light enough and when she was first introduced, she took to this seat right away. She likes the adventurous feeling of riding on the back of the bicycle and I feel good knowing that she is safe and secure.

Looking at the specifics of this Britax bicycle seat, the seat is very sturdy in construction and it takes about 20 minutes from the box to the point where it is ready to use. It fits most all bicycles with 26 to 28 inch wheels, which would be just about every adult bicycle manufactured. It has a built in suspension for your child's comfort and this can be a great asset if the roads or sidewalks in your area are full of potholes and bumps. The headrest has nine position settings, the footrest has fifteen positions, and the harness locks securely in place, for maximum safety. The padding can be removed and is machine washable, for added convenience, and the product carries a limited two- year warranty.

Going for a spin with a child in a small seat behind you is quite an adventure and it does take getting used to. The added weight means you have to be more careful when you stop, when you start, and how you maneuver because you always have to be mindful of the child behind you and their safety. I admit that I was a little anxious when I used this at first, but my anxiety quickly faded when I started to ride. Once you get the hang of it, like anything, it gets easier. And it is very fun for the small child in the back who gets to enjoy the sites and the excitement of riding out in the open.

All things considered, I am hard pressed to find anything wrong with this bicycle seat and I recommend it for those with small children who like the adventure and fitness they receive from riding a bicycle. I would like to ride more, and perhaps this bicycle seat will encourage me to get more active. The seat is solid in construction, fairly easy to install, and made with safety in mind. It has all the earmarks of another quality Britax product and it earns a easy recommendation.
text_fidelity_b: Britax Child Bike Seat (Prior Model)

Axiom Streamliner Road DLX Racks I am pleased with the rack. However, it did not come with any instructions. I was able to figure it out anyway. You have to take off your rear brake and mount the bracket on the brake bolt between the brake and the frame. You put your wheel skewer through the holes on the bottom. Note that this makes it annoying to remove the rear wheel.

As another reviewer noted, the bracket needs to be bent in order to fit. This is unavoidable because different bicycles have different frame geometry. It is easy to bend with pliers and I had it bent correctly in about 2 minutes.

Note also that it is a narrow rack and is meant for mounting bags or baskets on the sides. Mounting to the top is iffy. (I mounted a basket to the top anyway, using enough zip ties to make sure it won't move).

This rack is much more securely mounted than my old one, which was mounted with p-clips. It is also much lower and closer to the wheel which helps keep the weight down low so it doesn't affect handling as much.

If you have a road bike, you can definitely use this rack to increase your cargo capacity. I was looking for something like this for a while and I'm glad someone makes it.

text_fidelity_a:
Cathe Friedrich's Supersets & Push Pull DVD (Body Blast series) On this DVD, master instructor Cathe Friedrich offers two workouts from her Body Blast series: Supersets, a strength workout in which exercises are performed in rounds, and Push Pull, a strength workout focused on opposing muscle groups. Both workouts are very good, but what really makes this DVD so valuable is the wide variety of customization options as described below.

Supersets is a 53 minute workout. In each round, Cathe does separate exercises to work the legs, back, chest, shoulders/biceps/triceps, and core. After a brief (4-minute) warm-up, there are a total of two rounds, each broken down into two series (A and B). Cathe encourages participants to lift as heavy as possible, and she incorporates use of a barbell, dumbbells, a stability ball, and unweighted exercises as well. Many exercises are non-traditional in nature, as they include "low end" pluses as well as plyometric moves such as jump squats. The workout makes nice use of the stability ball, particularly for the core work, and Cathe finishes with 5.5 minutes of floor stretches.

Push Pull is a 45-minute, full-body weight training routine which works opposing muscle groups. In some cases, the muscle group is worked with only one exercise, whereas other muscles are targeted with several different exercises. Equipment used for this workout includes a tall step, a stability ball, a barbell, and several sets of dumbbells. The workout begins with a 3-minute warm-up which consists of some light cardio plus stretches using the tall step. Cathe then jumps right in on the legs, performing squats with the barbell, deadlifts, lunges (placing one heel on a smaller barbell to increase the work to the quads), and tall box presses. Moving on to the upper body, Cathe does chest press and rows, then ball work, includnig chest flyes and a "Y" move. Additional upper body work includes a shoulder press off the step, a one-arm row, a front raise while seated on the ball, a rear delt raise lying on the ball, bicep work with one leg on the ball for balance, and tricep dips/kickbacks. Cathe also incorporates the ball for floor leg work such as outer thigh lifts and inner thigh squeezes. There is also additional back work, abs work, and calf raises. Cathe concludes with a short (4.5 minutes) stretch that includes some nice shoulder stretches.

As mentioned above, the best thing about this DVD is the wide variety of custom options. The menus for both Supersets and Push Pull include options for playing the entire workout, viewing the chapter selections, and mixing and matching chapters. In addition, each workout offers "Quick Select Premixes" which provide both shorter and longer workout options. For Supersets, there are 14 premixes ranging in length from 28-109 minutes (these include extra cycles, upper/lower body only, etc.), and for Push Pull, there are 7 premixes ranging from 18-77 minutes which also included upper/lower body only options. Finally, there is a "Workout Blender" option which allows you to create your own custom workout by selecting chapters from either Supersets or Push Pull.

If you are familiar with Cathe, you know that she often incorporates upbeat, recognizable music (selections here include "Goldeneye," "Unbreak My Heart," "Walking in Memphis," and "Breakfast at Tiffany's"). Both workouts are solid, intermediate-level routines which will definitely help you to target virtually every body part from head-to-toe; my overall rating is 4 1/2 starts, and I would definitely recommend this DVD to others.
text_fidelity_b: Cathe Friedrich's Supersets & Push Pull DVD (Body Blast series)

ENGEL HD30 Waterproof Soft-Sided Cooler Tote Bag I'll be honest, I got this for ice cream transport. I spent days watching reviews, videos, and doing research months ahead of when I knew I'd be swinging by my favorite Ice Creamery for my biannual load-up on magically jersey-cow made ice cream. The fact that I needed a cooler to make grocery hauls in the summer, and for beach vacations and picnics and camping trips all came second.

I wanted something BIG! I was planning on getting 12-14 quarts of ice cream plus at least 4 large cooler shock ice packs. I don't care how heavy it is and I don't particularly care if I can sit on it.

I am 110% satisfied with this thing. It is rugged, attractive, reliable, and, if packed appropriately, can sit out in the beating sun for days.

This sucker is THICK, the top opening does take some wrangling to get bulky objects in/out, but not a deal breaker for me. The zipper is so satisfying I know I could dive with this thing.

The handles and straps and doohickeys are fine, I use the shoulder strap almost exclusively since I'm usually alone until I'm actually at a destination. I have narrow slightly sloping shoulders so it does slide a bit but it's comfortable. You can make this thing ridiculously heavy and there are no signs of straining of straps or stitching, only of your arm muscles.

So I first got to test it out going up to our cabin for 4th of July. I put frozen and fridge goods in it with only 3 of the large cooler shock ice packs. For 4.5 days it was like an extension of our small fridge/freezer, I did have to refreeze and add in the 4th after day 2 though because it wasn't very full. Bonus: it was also puppy proof on my puppy Jordi's first vacation!

Next step, the beach for a week. It worked phenomenally. I didn't use it as much on the beach because we lived so close to the beach and it was so hot it was pretty much only me most of the day down on the sand, but I was really impressed when it was trapped in the sun in my hot car for 16 hours on the first day and when I unzipped it smoke like frozen vapor came up and out.

I would highly recommend this product
text_fidelity_b: ENGEL HD30 Waterproof Soft-Sided Cooler Tote Bag

text_fidelity_a:
NordicTrack T Series Treadmills My primary concerned based on other reviews was that the motor would be noisy. That depends entirely on the speed. If you want it as a walking treadmill, you will definitely hear your footfalls much louder. You could whisper above the motor, no problem. If you are a casual runner and want to take it to say 6 miles an hour (that's pretty much a 30 minute 5K) it's quiet. You can sort of hear it, but not a lot. If you are a pro athlete and want to take it to 10 miles an hour, first off, respect, and second off, you will hear noise about the equivalent to a car engine on the highway.

The iFit attachment, which I recommend, doesn't come with it. You need to buy it, and the subscription, separately. It enables you to download a series of training programs via WiFi including what may be the world's easiest C25K program. They call it Beginner 5K. It's 4 times a week for 12 weeks. It starts with you casually strolling along on the treadmill for half a mile in 15 minute (think the average walking pace of a senior citizen) but it ends with you running uphill at about 5 miles an hour (at that rate you could finish a 5K in roughly 40 minutes) and there are no sudden transitions. It just creeps up the incline a little, then the speed, and soon the fast pace of the old level is the resting pace of the new, but it feels like a resting pace. You build fitness gradually. The treadmill has some pre-programmed routes and workouts built in, and the site has a great many more. My only complaint is there is no way to preview the list before subscribing, to know if it's worth it. Set up for that was a bit of a pain, more so than I'd expected.

I found the left speaker a little weaker than the right, but that could be an audio trick used by Zombies, Run! Otherwise, the sound system is nice. It plugs in via a standard audio cable, not Blutooth in an era where standard audio cables are going out of fashion. There are adapters if that becomes an issue. There are holders for water and phone, etc, and a nice ledge for an ipad.

I like the cushioning, and it is adjustable. I like how easy it is to fold up. Mind, assemble this where you mean to keep it. You're not going to fold it and stuff it in a closet. It's way too heavy for that. Installation takes two people, especially at the end when you have to hold the bottom unit up to install the hydraulic lift. I needed to check a video for that part.

The off switch is to take the little key off the panel. You can use the reset button on the bottom, if you've set it up to be conveniently accessible, but it takes a lot longer to come back from that. It actually takes longer to come back from that, than from shutting of the surge protector it's plugged into, which makes me think it is doing some sort of reset processing. It definitely needs a surge protected, and I recommend the NordicTrack brand for this, just to be safe.

Overall, I'd say this is a high quality treadmill at a reasonable price.
text_fidelity_b: NordicTrack T Series Treadmills

Note: although I cannot personally try it… A lot of varied lids fit between different water bottles.. so, that is certainly worth a try if, wanting to trade around lids (our wide mouth hydro was our bottle just recently lost.. and what I’m replacing.. so, I cannot try swapping that lead specifically to say for sure. But, just don’t rule it out!)

As for cold drinks… This is what we use ours for and it keeps things perfectly cold. We filled with 3/4 ice and water- then, checking 24 hours later… We still had ice!! As far as water bottles go I have confidence this will perform as one hopes it would, tiny dancer in a tutu and all!

2 other things FYI’s I want to share:

1. You can actually by water bottle ice trays- they look like a shape/size of a roll of coins and when frozen, they pop out and slide into water bottle with ease..This is a new discovery for us and as avid h2o bottle users- for a few $, it was a great investment. Pop a few into bottle and you’re good to go- super easy!! (you just have to remember to fill the ice tray each night!)

2. If using with any sugary or, flavored substance.. one should empty and rinse out bottle once done. Do not let it sit dirty in sink for a day or 2.. I’ve been told it compromises the integrity and taints the inside of the bottle- ever messing up the flavor moving forward. I also heard never to use with alcohol but… Haven't used in that realm- so, i’m sure if flavor won’t dissipate afterwards?

I hope this info can help in your decision… Feel free to let me know!

Fizik Performance Bicycle Bar Tape - Soft, Tacky & Classic Professional Bike Handlebar Tape (2mm, 2.7mm, 3mm) This is a review of the updated Fizik Tempo Microtex Classic (2mm) bar tape. I have been using the old Fizik performance 3mm tacky bar tape on both my road and CX/gravel bikes for several years now, and while that tape was pretty difficult to install (especially on irregular bar shapes) I really liked the look and feel of it and the durability.

This 2mm Microtex tape was much easier to wrap my aero bars with compared to the thick and tacky version I have been using.. but I do prefer the feel of the thicker tacky tape. I can't really speak to the durability of this tape since I've only had it for a few rides but it seems durable when installing it and appears to be easy to clean.

Unfortunately it seems Fizik no longer makes perforated 3mm tacky tape, the new iterations are either flat unperforated tape or grooved channels. I'm not a big fan of the grooved look of the Vento tapes but I may consider using the flat Terra version when I need to rewrap my CX bike.. I really wish they would release a tacky version of the Tempo perforated tape though as I much prefer that look.

I still have this, it’s held up quite well, and I definitely still use it. There is definitely a learning curve, and I still have trouble getting it in just the right spot to hand upside down without the fabric digging into me. BUT, once I AM n the right spot, I can hang there for 5-10 minutes and the benefits are great. I am overweight (but working on it!) and that definitely adds to the difficulty. There are so many other things that can be done with this prop though… my son was in a near fatal car accident, had many surgeries, and this device helped him immensely during his physical therapy. I’m leaving the negative stuff I wrote below just to be fully transparent. I really WAS disappointed at first, but I love it now
——————————————————
I am sad to be writing a negative review. I wanted one of these things for years! (A yoga swing, not necessarily this brand.) I bought this primarily for inverted poses to help with back pain. The cloth digs into my lower back and upper thighs terribly when I hang upside down... to the point of actual pain. I followed installation instructions; stood with my arms out, bent them up in a 90° angle and then installed the hardware to hang it from on the ceiling. I bought the suggested hardware. It feels as if this is too far apart, and I read installation instructions for another company's yoga swing which said to install the hardware no more and no less than 16" apart. Maybe this would help? I've tried bunching up the fabric and rearranging it in all different ways. If anyone has a suggestion I would be most grateful. For the price I paid (and when similar products cost HALF what this one does) I WANT to be happy with it. For now, I am extremely disappointed.

text_fidelity_a:
Osprey Packs Talon 11 Backpack, Flame Orange, Small/Medium I love this pack for hiking. Can't really fault it for anything. Only complaint is water bladder is a bit of a struggle to get inserted with water in it, even without water it's a bit tough. You just have to believe with all your heart that it will go in and it will, eventually.

I like the pack so much, I bought it's bigger brother the Talon 22. I really like the multiple ways I can lash my trekking poles to it and how useful the bungy cinch area is for carrying a variety of items. I used it recently to carry a litter sized water bottle when I needed more water than my bladder could carry.

I'm 6' and the M/L is plenty long. One of the reasons I got this pack is because of the two sizes available, and nice hip belt that can be hard to find on a small pack. In fact it's hard to find a real hiking pack in such a small size.

I bought a used one first and the buckle for the helmet holder/bungy cords was broken. The plastic seemed really flimsy. But the buckle on the new pack was much better. So give that buckle a few good squeezes to make sure you have a good buckle before heading out. Might be good to check all of them, if some aren't getting molded right.
text_fidelity_b: Osprey Packs Talon 11 Backpack, Flame Orange, Small/Medium

text_fidelity_a:
Coleman Cast Iron Grill Pan This 10" pre-seasoned cast iron grill pan by Coleman was offered at a very economical price as compared to similar items and meets the needs for which I intended to use it just fine. I needed a safe surface to do the final searing of sous vide steaks, chops and chicken for two so this is safe enough to handle the high intensity heat of the blow torch I use and sized is just right for a couple of steaks, chops, or chicken breasts at a time.

The sides are high enough to prevent my searing flame from flowing over the item and out of the pan area, the ribs contain the juices, and the pour spout makes draining easy. The handle is also cast iron so bear in mind that you need to wear oven mitts to protect your hands when cooking in the pan since it will get hot.

This pan is pre-seasoned, but that doesn't mean exactly the same thing as a non-stick coating. When it comes to cast iron pans, seasoning means a vegetable oil baked onto the iron at a high temperature which serves to protect the cast iron from moisture which would lead to the pan rusting, and also serves as a natural non-stick film for easy release of the item you're cooking.

You might want to add a little butter or oil if you're cooking eggs in the new pan however since the best non-stick benefits of seasoning haven't had a chance to really build up yet. After using this pan you should hand wash it, dry it completely, and then rub it with a light coating of vegetable oil on it to restore a sheen.

The more you use the pan and re-season it the better the non-stick tendency will be, and that's why a lot of folks love finding old cast iron pans at yard sales. Those old pans that were lovingly used & cared for over a long time had years to get well seasoned. If you take care of this one it should serve you well over the years so I'd gladly recommend it.
text_fidelity_b: Coleman Cast Iron Grill Pan

text_fidelity_a: BYER OF MAINE, Pangean Glider Chair, Green, Now Partially Assembled, Perfect for Camping, Matching Furniture 38" D X 25" W X 39" H For starters I found this chair difficult to assemble.  The instructions looked like they'd taken a bad copy and reproduced it many times.  There was little definition of the diagrams.  It would've helped to be able to see the slots and bolt holes more clearly so you would know if you have the piece oriented correctly.  A couple of mistakes I made had to be corrected.  It took more than an hour to assemble what should've taken 15-20 minutes with instructions that were clear.  I found a You Tube that helped a bit though it had no sound and was in fast motion.  Another review mentioned arms would be nice, and I agree with that but it would be difficult to incorporate and not inline with the style of a sling chair.  So I subtracted a star for assembly difficulty. I also didn't find the chair to be all that comfortable, and because you stay in a reclining position it's not conducive to anything but laying back and relaxing.  Nothing wrong with relaxing, but having a cup of coffee or soda would be very clumsy unless you leaned forward to sip or drink.  And you would not be on eye level for conversation with others.  So I subtracted a star for this.  The quality however is very nice.  The wood is beautiful and once assembled it's very sturdy and you can tell it will last a long time.  I can see where others would give this 5 stars...particularly if they has someone assemble it for them and they found it to be more comfortable.  One more thing in closing...I considered this as a beach chair but a better application would be on a deck or by the pool.  It's not as light and convenient to carry as a conventional beach chair.

text_fidelity_a:
Gym Timer with Remote, Alrigon LED Interval Timer Clock 1.5" Digits Down/Up Clock Stopwatch for Crossfit, Tabata, EMOM, MMA I got this timer for not only workouts, but also for using in organizing my time. I have to balance art work with home office work so I need to have a timer to help me not go over schedule for these different things. Let's take a look at this timer.

MANUAL
The manual that comes with this is very well laid out. I am extremely impressed with it. There are many photos which are helpful in the remote and wall installation as well as excellent information on how to run this timer in various modes.

LEARNING CURVE- GIVE YOURSELF TIME TO LEARN
I highly suggest that you take some time to learn this timer before you try to use it. I know that sounds silly, but there is a learning curve to this. I found it much nicer when I took the time to learn each function, play with it and then make notes in the manual. If you are already familiar with this type of timer, of course, then you probably won't need that.

CORDS
This came with TWO cords. One of them is a USB cord which is 3 ft long. That will plug into any USB port. The 2nd is a plug that has a transformer on the end. It is a sideways plug so it should fit on most power strips. That cord is only 68 inches long.

REMOTE
You will need two AAA batteries. This did not come with any. The manual has extensive instructions on how to set up and use the remote. They are very visual so visual learners will love this. It is IR and will work from across an average room, not sure about a large gym, however.

CLOCK
You can set this up as a real time clock and then use it as a timer so you don't have to unplug it when you are done. The timers all set up individually outside of the clock which keeps running in the background.

TIMER
The timer is easy to see from anywhere around my basement room or upstairs if I am using it in a room for other purposes. It does have a loud alarm on it too. I use the timer, Count Up and Count Down settings the most. I use interval timing when I want to follow a tight schedule during the day.

DOES IT PERFORM WELL?
I am very happy with this timer. I love that it has TWO cords so that I can put it on the table top when I am doing artwork. I can plug it into my USB outlet which is very close and then have the timer nearby. When I want to use this in the workout setting, I move it to my basement and either attach it to an outlet, or if I don't have one near where I want to use it, I use a power bank.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This timer is easy to see, great to operate, and extremely helpful in daily workouts or schedules. I am glad to have it and appreciate the work that went into the manual too. There is some learning to this timer, however. If you have never had one before, plan on taking some time to learn the set up.

MY RATING
FIVE STARS. This is a great set up. I use this a lot.
text_fidelity_b: Gym Timer with Remote, Alrigon LED Interval Timer Clock 1.5" Digits Down/Up Clock Stopwatch for Crossfit, Tabata, EMOM, MMA

text_fidelity_a:
Lite Holster Stretch, Expandable, Secure Flashlight Holder with Belt Clip, Universal Sizing, Black My use is for 1" diameter by 5" long tactical lights which do not protrude out the bottom. I also tried it with a 2 C cell light which protrudes out the bottom a lot.

I was looking for something either with a flap cover or a snug but easy to insert fit. This is neither. It has no cover flap, but has a VERY snug fit on this type of light. However it is made up of a series of internal flaps and elastic straps you have to guide the light through to get it into this case. You cannot easily do this one handed as you have to spread two internal flaps apart and hold them that way to insert the light. In addition if you have to sit/stand as in driving patrol or the like, the light works it's way out the top even if it doesn't protrude out the bottom. Since there is nothing to lock it in, the movement of sitting and moving around when seated pushes against the bottom squeezing the light upward like squeezing a toothpaste tube. Eventually it pops out the top. In addition if your light has a tailcap switch it will get turned on without your knowing it in daytime (you would see the light at night), draining the batteries, as there is nothing protecting the tailcap switch from being pressed against the seat bottom.

From my experience with it, this is pretty useless if you are going to be wearing it on a belt in the vertical position, whether a short small diameter or longer larger diameter light. As a temporary worklight holder it isn't bad, but how often do you need a worklight on your belt?
text_fidelity_b: Lite Holster Stretch, Expandable, Secure Flashlight Holder with Belt Clip, Universal Sizing, Black

text_fidelity_a:
Universal Bicycle Rear Seat Cushion Armrest Footrest Set, Kids Child Safety Carrier Bicycle Baby Seat, Including Cushion and Backrest, Armrest Handrail, Footrests, Bell As soon as I put this on my bike, my kids wanted to go for a ride. They took turns for the next hour or so. Before this, I had my son riding on a towel on my rear rack. He would hold my seat post and most of the time bury his face in my back so that he wouldn't fall off. He also had to hold his legs out so that his feet wouldn't get caught in the chain or the tire. With this seat, he can sit back in comfort, he has his own little handlebars to hold, and the seat is nice and soft for him. He is extremely happy that I got this for him.

Installation was a little difficult, but nothing crazy. I would have loved a second pair of hands to help me install, but the rest of my family was suddenly busy when I started putting it on. The only part that was hard was getting the crossbar on under the rack. One of the support beams would be right next to the bar, no matter how I installed the seat. It took a little maneuvering, but I managed to wedge the crossbar in and get the seat bolted down. Even if a nut falls off, I don't think the seat will move because of the way it is wedged on. So I feel it's very safe. One thing I wouldn't mind is having the brace that holds the backrest be a little more sturdy.

It's been a few weeks now and so far everything has held up. The bike was left out in the rain a few times, but I don't notice any rust appearing. I'm pretty pleased with this purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Universal Bicycle Rear Seat Cushion Armrest Footrest Set, Kids Child Safety Carrier Bicycle Baby Seat, Including Cushion and Backrest, Armrest Handrail, Footrests, Bell
